operations.title: Research state for replicable PAC sample complexity
operations.summary: The central question is the worst-case replicable PAC sample complexity for finite classes. For fixed sufficiently small positive confidence parameters, the current global comparison remains between a soft lower bound of order (log N)^(3/2)/epsilon and an upper bound of order (log N)^2/epsilon. The uniform cyclic-half-interval results do not improve either side of this exponent gap. The root has one durable restricted program and no active unreconciled dispute.

operations.title: Uniform cyclic half-interval replicability
operations.summary: Studies exact-output replicable learning of the k cyclic translates of a half-interval on Z_k when the unlabeled distribution is fixed to be uniform. The program contains a proper upper bound, an unrestricted-learner lower bound, a confidence-qualified matching characterization, a weak worst-case corollary, a distributional limitation on the absence of log k dependence, and a coordinatewise tensorization heuristic. It supplies no arbitrary-distribution upper bound or improvement to the global logarithmic exponent.

operations.title: Proper replicable upper bound under the uniform distribution
operations.summary: For odd k, there is a proper learner for H_k under the uniform distribution on Z_k. With q equal to ceil(k/(floor(epsilon k/2)+1)), accuracy and exact-output replicability hold when n is at least max{epsilon^(-1) log(2/delta), 4q/rho}. Since q<2/epsilon+1<=3/epsilon, it suffices that n is at least max{epsilon^(-1) log(2/delta), 12/(epsilon rho)}. This is only a fixed-uniform-distribution upper bound.

operations.title: Uniform-distribution lower bound against unrestricted learners
operations.summary: For odd k, if 0<epsilon<=1/4, 0<delta,rho<=1/20, and k>=1/(5 epsilon rho), every randomized, computationally unbounded, possibly improper learner that is accurate and replicable for every target in H_k under the fixed uniform distribution requires n>=1/(120 epsilon rho). The restriction is to the fixed uniform distribution, not to proper, efficient, or deterministic learners.

operations.title: Confidence-qualified sample-complexity characterization
operations.summary: In the lower-bound regime, n_unif lies between 1/(120 epsilon rho) and max{epsilon^(-1) log(2/delta), 12/(epsilon rho)}. Hence n_unif=Theta(1/(epsilon rho)) for fixed sufficiently small delta and rho, and more generally when log(2/delta)=O(1/rho). This characterization is not established uniformly for arbitrarily small delta because no matching confidence-dependent lower bound is supplied.

operations.title: Worst-case lower-bound corollary from the uniform experiment
operations.summary: In the stated parameter regime, the uniform lower bound transfers to n_rep(k,epsilon,delta,rho)>=1/(120 epsilon rho), because a worst-case learner must also work for the uniform distribution. The fixed-uniform upper bound does not transfer. The corollary has no growing log k factor and does not improve the established global lower baseline.

operations.title: Scope of the absence of a growing alphabet-size cost
operations.summary: For fixed epsilon, delta, and rho, the proper upper bound under the uniform distribution is independent of k. Thus the uniform one-coordinate mechanism does not itself generate a growing log k sample cost. This does not establish the same conclusion for arbitrary or adversarial nonuniform distributions on Z_k, and it is not a global hardness classification of H_k.

operations.title: Naive coordinatewise tensorization scaling
operations.summary: If a d-coordinate construction supplied about n/d samples per coordinate, the one-coordinate boundary estimate would suggest per-coordinate instability of order d/(n epsilon), total mismatch of order d^2/(n epsilon), and a naive sample scale d^2/(epsilon rho). Random coordinate counts and possible global structure prevent this calculation from establishing either an upper or lower bound; it is only a heuristic lead.
